title: Herbicide-resistant weeds
bottleneck: Weeds have evolved resistance to nearly all major herbicide modes of action, with glyphosate-resistant superweeds now infesting millions of hectares; weed control consumes a large share of farm labor and chemical budgets worldwide. New herbicide chemistry has essentially stalled — no new mode of action in decades — leaving mechanical and cultural control, which don't scale to industrial farming, as the fallback. New herbicide chemistry has essentially stalled - no new mode of action in decades - leaving non-scalable fallbacks.
why_it_blocks: Weeds cut yields by competing for light, water, and nutrients. Losing chemical control threatens the economics of large-scale grain production. Losing chemical control threatens the economics of large-scale grain production.
current_state: Integrated weed management is preached but rarely practiced at scale; the chemistry pipeline is dry.
